  MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  CITY OF NORWALK
  PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  May 6, 2024

Chair Greenidge called the meeting to order at 6:02 p.m. in the Council Chambers,
Norwalk City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Responding to the roll
call were Commissioner Apodaca, Commissioner Fernandez-Silva, Chair Greenidge,
Commissioner Hoskins, Commissioner Knieling, Vice Chair LeGaspi, Commissioner Dr.
Rodriguez, and Commissioner Rosoff. Also present were Ozzie Ramos, Director of
Public Safety, Berenia Orozco, Management Analyst, and Sheriff’s Deputy Dave
Vivona.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Chair Greenidge called for the approval of the Public Safety commission meeting
minutes that was held on March 4, 2024, and April 1, 2024.

MOTION CARRIED BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

AYES:  Commissioner Apodaca, Commissioner Fernandez-Silva, Chair
  Greenidge, Commissioner Hoskins, Commissioner Knieling, Vice
  Chair LeGaspi, Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez, and Commissioner
  Rosoff
NOES:  None
ABSENT: Commissioner Pena
ABSTAIN: None

REPORTS

Mrs. Orozco presented Mr. Ozzie Ramos to give a brief update for the Public Safety
Department. Mr. Ramos introduced the Sheriff’s Deputy Dave Vivona and shared what
a tremendous job he has done as a traffic deputy in our city. He has been working for
the city for about 24 years and has addressed all types of traffic complaints and
incidents.

Deputy Vivona shared his experience in working traffic and explained the process of
being able to report incidents accurately and quickly. He shared that as traffic deputies,
they need to stay within the state ration of enforcement without over enforcing and
writing more tickets than there are accidents. He shared that the more enforcement is
provided, the better results we have in preventing collisions. He stated that they can
better provide their services if residents can share the concerns they have in their
neighborhoods.
 Minutes of the Regular Meeting
Norwalk Public Safety Commission
May 6, 2024

Deputy Vivona shared that they have a Directive Patrol Missions where Public Safety
meets with the traffic team to share residents shared concerns from either contacting
the Public Safety office, Neighborhood Watch Meetings, or elsewhere. From there, they
will patrol the area to investigate whether it is indeed a problem and may cite people for
violations when they are present. They emphasize their presence to prevent further
nuisances for a few weeks.

These meetings are meant to keep track of the city’s nuisances. When it comes to traffic
nuisances, he focuses on education through social media and advising parents of the
violations. He also enforces and addresses violations such as minibikes and speeding
in the city. Vice Chair LeGaspi asked what the best way to report problems to the
sheriff’s department and Deputy Vivona shared that they are able to reach the Public
Safety office and request action from LASD. The NET (Norwalk Enforcement Team) will
focus on crime, traffic, code etc. and see which department is most suitable to address
and will be discussed at the NET meeting. This problem is added to our database where
we can discuss initiatives and updates on a weekly basis then will be removed once it is
resolved in the best way possible.

Commissioner Rosoff also brought up the idea of contacting their quadrant officer in the
area to have them relay their concern to the NET. Deputy Vivona shared that Quadrant
Officers are also an excellent resource and will also ensure that a NET member is
addressing issues of reported crime and traffic.

Mr. Ramos thanked Deputy Vivona and addressed the issue of DUI’s and how the City
of Norwalk is working to address them. This year, the city has had two DUI operations
with the goal of deterring people from drinking and driving and saving lives. Additionally,
in March, we had instances where pedestrians were struck by vehicles which led to our
Traffic operation in stationing deputies at the Studebaker Rd corridor. We had
undercover officers crossing a crosswalk and the motorists failing to yield were cited
which resulted in issuing about 28 tickets. Mr. Ramos proceeded to update the
commission on the enhancements being made to the 105 Fwy Exit & Studebaker
offramp. He thanked the commissioners, the leadership in the community and the
partnership with our stakeholders for their attention to this matter and their push to
make improvements. Lastly, Mr. Ramos welcomed newly appointed commissioner Ms.
Kim Apodaca to the Public Safety Commission.

Vice Chair Legaspi asked Deputy Vivona about his opinion regarding speedbumps.
Deputy Vivona shared his opinion regarding the effectiveness of speedbumps and
spoke about the effect of speedbumps in local neighborhoods and the way they divert
traffic. Mr. Ramos thanked Deputy Vivona for sharing his opinion and reminded the
commission on the City’s position on speed bumps. He reminded the commission that if
speed bumps are designed and placed in the correct areas and enforcement action is
taken, they can be an effective calming measure to reduce speeding in neighborhoods.
  2
 Minutes of the Regular Meeting
Norwalk Public Safety Commission
May 6, 2024

From a quality-of-life perspective, this resource is something that should be shared with
community members. Mr. Ramos proceeded to share with the commission the
qualifying criteria for speed bumps: street width must be less than 36 ft, speed limit
must be 25 mph or less, one lane in each direction, grade of 5% or less, not a major
thoroughfare, City cannot be a regional transit bus route, and on top of this a petition
must be signed from community members.

Mr. Ramos spoke on his commitment to Public Safety and the Transportation Center.
He mentioned the department’s effort to engage the community and commuters who
use our Transportation center. He shared positive feedback that was received from the
public during the Coffee with a Commuter event that was held at the transportation
center that morning.

Lastly, Mr. Ramos briefly went over the Public Safety Activities Memo that was rolled
out that month. He explained that this memo was created in an effort to be more
transparent with the commission about the efforts of the department to keep the
community safe. This memo will contain statistics of the department and will be emailed
on the last working day of the month.

STAFF COMMENTS

Mrs. Orozco went over the May 2024 calendar.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS
Commissioner Apodaca inquired about speed bumps and whether they can be removed
after being installed. A follow-up will be conducted on this inquiry.

Commissioner LeGaspi reminded the commissioners of the “Commissioner Meet &
Greet event.

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

There was no one wishing to address the Public Safety commission.

ADJOURNMENT:

Being no further business to come before the Public Safety Commission, the meeting
was adjourned at 6:40 PM.
